**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The licence grant to Sanofi (Section 3.1(a), p0248) meets the preferred position on every material term:

- **Scope:** exclusive even as to RevMed and its Affiliates, royalty-bearing, covering Research, Development, Manufacture and full Commercialization of Products, in the "Field" (defined as *any and all uses*) and the "Licensed Territory" (*all countries and territories of the world*).
- **Affiliates and contractors:** Section 3.4(a) lets us act through any Affiliate without RevMed's consent; 3.4(b) permits sublicensing through multiple tiers (only a U.S. "substantially all" sublicense needs consent, which cannot be unreasonably withheld); 3.4(c)(i) permits subcontracting to Third Parties as we deem appropriate.
- **Not revocable at will:** RevMed may terminate only for uncured material breach (p0491), insolvency (p0492), or the negotiated Competing Product / cessation triggers (p0493, p0495), each with notice and cure.
- **Transferability:** Section 15.2(a)(i)–(ii) permits assignment without consent to our Affiliates and to a successor in an M&A or substantially-all-assets transaction.

Noted but not flagged: Affiliate/contractor rights are located in Section 3.4 rather than in the grant language itself, and the U.S. mega-sublicense consent plus the Acquiror-Family IP carve-outs (p0612) are minor frictions that fall short of a material deviation.
